newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Reformist wins important Russian regional poll.
newsitem.headline: Reformist wins important Russian regional poll.

text.p: Reformist Ivan Sklyarov beat a communist rival to be elected governor of the Nizhny Novgorod region, according to provisional final results on Monday from an election seen as a test of Russia's reforms.
"Fifty-two percent voted for Sklyarov and 42 percent voted for Gennady Khodyrev," an election commission spokesman said following Sunday's election.

The turnout was 49 percent in the run-off vote. The two rivals finished ahead of the field in the first round of voting in the region east of Moscow two weeks ago, but neither won enough votes then for outright victory.

Sklyarov, 49, has until now been the mayor of Nizhny Novgorod. He was backed by reformists in the Kremlin including Boris Nemtsov, Nizhny Novgorod's governor until he was summoned to join the Russian government in March to boost reforms.

The opposition comunists and some nationalists had backed Khodyrev, a former regional leader in Soviet times, and the vote had been seen as an informal referendum on the country's transition to a market economy.
"This result clearly shows that the population backs government reforms," local television Seti NN said.
